body: The new `lineage` event kind joins the event kinds in the core crate only, never Claude-named, and its line follows the event line contract; it is written once by the wrapper as the one writer of that instance's event log.

The `viola list` board keeps its six captions, their words and slot order fixed by literal; the fleet trees are drawn inside those fixed columns and the caption order and board structure stay as pinned.
The tree form of `viola list` is static linear output: no spinner, no cursor movement, a parent-child relation readable from printed text and order, not from layout or colour alone.

Plain when piped: with stdout not a colour-capable terminal the tree and link views carry no SGR at all; on a terminal any SGR sits only beside its printed word (bold only on NAME values, dim only on stale rows, amber only on the DIALOG word), colour only a second cue.
The board's empty-board line, the unwrapped separator `-- UNWRAPPED - READ-ONLY --` and NAME truncation rules hold with the trees drawn; unwrapped sessions carry no lineage.

Observed links shown apart from parent edges: a link name is printed only after it parses as a viola name, printed names being the parsed arguments, and any C0/C1 control bytes in a printed name or role are escaped.
The 0.1.0 `link` / `unlink` verbs keep their result line, `--json` output and exit 20 / 21 contracts; link pairs stay validated by the wrapper, and a parent edge is never a link.
A parent edge never changes whether a `send` is accepted: the send refusals (input-not-ready, no-prompt-submitted) and the wheel rules stay unchanged by lineage.

The launch-time parent declaration on `viola run`: any new flag shows in `viola --help` under its group label with the usage line, and any refusal it adds (an undeclarable or unparsable parent) is an operator fork that, if taken, follows the refusal layout: unable line with a kebab-case code word, hint line, exit code, one clean `--json` document with no hint, no stack trace.
Writing the lineage line at launch adds zero viola bytes to the TUI passthrough terminal; run diagnostics of the lineage write never reach the terminal, and human keystrokes are never blocked by it.

`viola revive` keeps the recorded parent: the revive human and `--json` refusals and `revive --list` rows and `--json` keep their contracts; any parent shown on `revive --list` follows the same name-check and escaping.
`list --json` payload: any lineage field it gains is an operator fork; a `--json` document stays one clean document with no SGR and no hint.
The log identity tags (process, service_name) on any new log line of the lineage write and read-back.
Time bounds never fall on the human: any bound on reading a parent at launch falls on the driver, never a harsh timeout on the user.
Proof without a live start: the measurements and checks come from tests or no-start probes; live readings never gate, and the boundary tests are sequenced on records, not on screen content.

body: A new `lineage` event kind: added only in the core crate, agent-neutral and never Claude-named, its wire value kebab-case, its line held to the event line shape (v, timestamp, source, data) and given its own event data per kind.

The wrapper is the one writer of the lineage line, appended once at start into that instance's own events log, one write per line, at a place in the start order where a failed start leaves no half-registered instance.

The lineage reads back the same after a crash and a replay: the snapshot replay recovers it as a log-derived field, a torn last line is healed by the next append, and an older reader meeting the new kind or field tolerates it (versioned tolerant records, missing equals null, skipped lines counted).

A parent declared at launch through `viola run`: its CLI argument style, the declared name parsed as a viola name and refused, never stripped, on control characters; which names, sockets or records a starting wrapper can see of its parent (its environment, the child environment names) is P3's first measurement.
A reused name never inherits an old parent: identity is by instance, never by name or location, and the existing refusals of a start over a held, live or stale name stay as they are.
`revive` keeps the parent its lineage recorded: revive goes in place through the start path, reads the snapshot once, and must carry the recorded parent rather than re-declare one.

A parent edge is a drawing label only: it never changes who holds the wheel, never adds or removes a link (the link set changes only on implicit links and link calls and follows the log), and never decides whether a send is accepted or refused.

`viola list` as fleet trees: the board's six fixed captions, their words and slot order unchanged; plain when stdout is not a terminal, with colour variables deciding only SGR output; list stays a caller-side read of state with no wrapper, without pagination, and the whole board is still refused on one failed check.

The board contract shared by CLI list and MCP list and the list payload items: what `list --json` gains is an operator fork, and any new field keeps snake_case names, declared key order and absent optional fields omitted.

Observed links drawn apart from parent edges on every view that shows both, and a link name shown only after it parses as a viola name; a name read from disk is untrusted upstream text, sanitised before any human line.

Every new closed word, event kind, field, column, refusal, time bound or split is a fork for the operator, written priced into one block of the run's founder-forks file at P3's end; every master row the change reaches is named after a search of all seven masters.

Disk and privacy of the new record: what the lineage line writes to disk, what of it outlives a SIGKILL (crash-safe writes, never-rotated events log), and what of a parent's identity lands in a file another session can read (content-bearing detail only in the instance, file mode set before any byte, codes-only process logs) are stated at P3.
Any new log line goes through the one event emitter into the obs event catalog and carries codes only, never a parent's name or role text.
Whether the new kind or payload field bumps the protocol version follows the protocol-version bump rule and mixed-version tolerance between an older and a newer binary on one home.

Proof under the directive: measurements from tests or no-start probes only — no live start, no rig start of a real claude, no witness run, no mutation run in this phase; the tests run against the fake agent in isolated viola homes.
The live-host leg of the lineage registry capability (the overseers run wrapped with their parents declared) cannot be proved here; whether it is claimable whole is read at P4/P5.

body: A new `lineage` event kind in the core event kinds, never Claude-named, carried on the standard event line: its format, keys, event kind round-trip and ts, and its data keys.
The lineage line written once at wrapper start by the wrapper as the single writer of its own event log, and its place in the run start events order and the first records of a start.
Lineage read back the same after a crash and a replay: the snapshot read-or-replay path, the replayed field set, replay writing no file, a torn tail healed by the next append.
The parent declaration at launch through `viola run`: the CLI argument and its refusals, the declared parent name parsed as a viola name, the leading-slash and control-character rules on argv.
A reused name never inherits an old parent: a start's lines are read from its own start offset, so a parent belongs to one instance's launch, not to its name.
`viola revive` keeps the recorded parent: the revive start path, its preflight order, its exit codes and refusal codes held as they are.
A parent edge is a drawing label only: the wheel at start, the link and unlink methods, and the send and answer refusal order stay unchanged by any parent.
`viola list` human board drawn as trees in the fixed columns: the board columns and captions, the unwrapped separator, stale rows dim, list names and rows escaping control characters.
Plain when piped: no SGR and no escape bytes in `viola list` output when stdout is not a terminal; SGR asserted only through an outer PTY.
`list --json`: one JSON document per run, its items, skipped counts and name fields, its mirror of the channel; any new field a fork for the operator.

Observed links shown apart from parent edges on every view showing both, a link name shown only after it parses as a viola name (raw-channel link name validation, link since kept, links surviving a wrapper restart).
The board held to the read rule: list reads a live wrapper through the replay, a board refusal opens no log, the strict-modes check before any read.
Unknown events counted and skipped: readers built before the new kind tolerate the `lineage` line, forward-compatible lines skipped.

What the lineage record writes to disk, what outlives a SIGKILL of the wrapper, and what of a parent's identity lands in a file another session can read, stated at P3: owner-only file modes, no session names in the wrapper log, logs carry no secrets.
Every new closed word, event kind, field, column, refusal or time bound is a closed-enum change that needs a decision: written as an operator fork at P3, never closed in code alone.
Measurements at P3 come from a test or a no-start probe over the fake agent: no live start, no real claude CLI, no rig start, no mutation or witness run in this phase.
